# Introduction
## Importance of predator-prey interactions to understand marine ecosystems

However, it's difficult to observe concurrently. Simultaneous observations of marine predators and prey fish remain challenging because predators may avoid large research vessels, and predator–prey interactions may occur outside their sampling coverage. Consequently, relatively few studies have documented concurrent, fine-scale predator–prey interactions in the field [@nottestad2002].
\
\
\

## Limited information from the previous studies about predator-prey interactions
Field-based evidence remains limited, although such evidence is important for understanding anti-predator strategies and how these behaviours affect predators’ access to fish. 
Vessel-based surveys is not optimal.

\
\
\

## Potential aid from USVs

However, no events have been reported
The opportunistic Saildrone observations of dolphins and seabirds provide an opportunity to examine whether fish-school characteristics differ between periods of predator presence and absence. 
\
\
\

## Acoustic characteristics of marine mammals and sandeel
\
\
\


## Objectives
We quantify differences in school depth, acoustic density, size, vertical extent, and shape.

 - Is vertical distribution and school density differ by predator type? Non-predator vs dolphins vs seabirds
 - School density (and vertical distribution) vs distance to predators
 - When is the most risky time? time of day, time of year
